direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels like a modern take on the 28 Days Later guerilla style with its advanced technology, as you can see the maturity and experience Danny Boyle gained after over 20 years; The direction on a macroscale is even more experimental than the already experimental film, but this kind of made the movie a bit corny and annoying at points; The direction on a microscale is good as all the interpersonal scenes are well executed, as you get to know these characters and how they experience the quarantine differently; The storytelling feels more polished and structured than the first film, but this may be due to Boyle's maturity as a filmmaker; He builds tension similarly to the first film

performance.comments: Shows how much of a well-trained actress she is, as her performance is full of emotions and she has good chemistry with the cast
Shows his charisma and experience playing the lead in big-budget action movies as he carries the scenes he is in and has good chemistry with Williams to create a father-son dynamic
The true lead of the film holds his own well as he acts well beyond his age and carries the story
Shows his experience as an actor as he is a real scene-stealer and makes his castmates better with his presence

cast.comments: The supporting actors are better this time around as there really isn't a bad performance; the infected are still infected, but they are packing this time around

story.comments: The concept is what would happen to Britain 28 years later, exploring how society devolves and the country is ravaged by the infected who mutate; The plot at the end of the day is about a son trying to help his mother, going on a journey to help her find a cure; The plot structure feels like a hero's journey mixed with infected/zombie elements, with a cliffhanger ending to set up the next movie; Character writing is pretty good, as you care about these characters and what they are experiencing

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is well-written and less corny; the symbolism is not as strong this time around, but the movie does touch on familial dynamics and the effects of a pandemic and how societies form after a loss of government; the foreshadowing is pretty good and helps set the ending and the exposition to lead into the next film

score.comments: Helps set the tension and tone for this movie to be an experimental infected movie, but it's a shame they didn't include any of the iconic themes from the original movie

cinematography.comments: The use of iPhones to shoot this movie feels eerie compared to the original film using camcorders because it is a modern way of making a guerilla-style movie that the original was known for; I really enjoyed a lot of the nature and drone shots as they helped build the world; I hated and got really annoyed by the death shots because the multiple angles made this movie feel like Fallout with its death sequences; I do understand what they shot this on, but widescreen for a blockbuster movie in the big 2025 is crazy

editing.comments: Made the movie have a guerilla feel that the original was known for; but the different cuts for the death sequences and some other edits made this movie feel annoying and tacky at points, even though I do get that this is an experimental movie

sound.comments: Feels like they used the budget and advanced technology to make this movie feel like a scary zombie or infected movie

visual_effects.comments: Feels like they used the budget and advanced technology to make this movie feel like a scary zombie or infected movie; some of the most daunting visuals I have seen in a zombie or infected movie

production_design.comments: Opted for a more natural, rural look instead of the abandoned urban sets in the first movie, and I think this was the right choice as it helped aid society in going back to live without technology and capitalism, so when they sprinkle in modern aspects it genuinely shocks the characters; The bone sets were well made and will become iconic for this franchise

makeup.comments: Helped paint the infected and feel more advanced than the last movies; They made the infected PACKED in this movie

costumes.comments: Helped paint the effect and feel more advanced than the last movies

review.pacing: Pacing is a little bit on the slower side for the first 50 minutes because of all the experimental aspects, but it really picks up in the second half with the right pace
review.climax: Climax is well executed and really closes the movie well; the coda at the end really just feels like a post-credit scene to lead into the next film
review.tone: Tone is a modern version of the post-apocalyptic tone created in the original movie, as the movie uses advanced technology and techniques to create the same guerilla style; The movie is an experimental version of an already experimental movie, as they really go left field sometimes with the edits and sequences they include
review.overall: Overall, a pretty good revival of the 28 Days Later franchise, as Danny Boyle and Alex Garland use their experience and maturity as filmmakers, coupled with more advanced technology, to recreate the guerilla post-apocalyptic feel in a more modern approach; the new experimental sequences in what is an already experimental franchise felt tacky and got really annoying at times
